name: Familial Hypokalemic Periodic Paralysis with Cardiac Arrhythmia
aliases: Familial Hypokalemic Periodic Paralysis and Cardiac Dysrhythmia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Hypokalemic Periodic Paralysis with Cardiac Arrhythmia

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of muscle weakness or paralysis associated with low serum potassium levels
Serum potassium concentration below 3.5 mmol/L during attacks
Electrocardiographic evidence of cardiac arrhythmias such as ventricular tachycardia or atrioventricular block
Positive family history of similar episodes or confirmed genetic mutation
Identification of pathogenic mutations in CACNA1S or SCN4A genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent hypokalemic paralysis episodes with documented hypokalemia and cardiac arrhythmia evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Typically triggered by rest after exercise or high carbohydrate meals
Includes ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation

common.notes: May occur during or outside paralysis episodes

occasional.notes: May cause breathing difficulties during severe attacks
Psychological distress due to unpredictable episodes

rare.notes: Reported in chronic cases with arrhythmia
Due to muscle fiber degeneration after repeated attacks

laboratory: Normal to low serum potassium between attacks
Elevated creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Cardiac MRI may reveal fibrosis in chronic cases
other: ECG abnormalities including prolonged QT interval and ventricular ectopy
Electromyography showing reduced muscle excitability during attacks

distinguishingFeatures: Episodes associated with elevated serum potassium

redFlags: Sudden onset of paralysis with cardiac arrhythmia
references: Statland JM, Tawil R. Hypokalemic periodic paralysis. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Tricarico D, Mele A. Familial hypokalemic periodic paralysis: pathophysiology and treatment. Neurol Sci. 2019;40(10):2049-2057.
Plaster NM, Tawil R, Tristani-Firouzi M, et al. Mutations in Kir2.1 cause the developmental and episodic muscle disease Andersen-Tawil syndrome. Cell. 2001;105(4):511-519.
